en.title: Total Time When Tasks of the Same Original Duration Are Halved Each Time
en.description:
Tasks run in their original order. Tasks with the same original duration belong to the same group; each time a task runs, the current duration of every other not-yet-run task in its group becomes half of that task's current duration, rounded up. Tasks whose original durations differ but later become equal cannot be grouped.

The standard I/O and the solution were written independently by this site; ranges marked as this site's are not the original source constraints.
en.input: The first line contains n, and the second line contains n initial durations. The original snapshot gives no upper bounds; the import catalog lists n≤100000, and this site extends it to 1≤n≤200000 with durations in 1..10^9.
en.explanation: Example 1: the actual times are 5, 3, 3, 6, 2, 2, for a total of 21. Example 2: 1 halved and rounded up is still 1, for a total of 3. Example 3: the three tasks take 4, 2, 2, for a total of 8; the initial 2 is not grouped with the 4 that was later reduced to 2.
hints: Keep a dictionary keyed by original duration storing the group's next execution time; take it out and add it to the total, then update it to half, rounded up.
